title: Chickenpox vaccine
what: A vaccine shot that protects against chickenpox. Usually two shots are needed.
why: For children who have not had chickenpox, and adults without immunity. Sometimes in the first days after contact with a sick person.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If you are ill now or have a fever
Immune system conditions, or treatment that weakens immunity
If you are pregnant or planning a pregnancy
If you had contact with someone with chickenpox, and when

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when the person is well.

prepare.title: After contact
prepare.text: If there was contact with a sick person, come as soon as possible, usually within the first 3 days.

prepare.title: Pregnancy
prepare.text: For women: it is best to avoid getting pregnant for a month after the vaccine.

steps: The doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped, and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in your documents
After the shot, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes soreness at the spot for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes, 1 to 3 weeks later, a few blisters or a fever
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
If blisters appear, avoid pregnant women and people with weak immunity until they dry up
The second dose follows the schedule
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services

faq.q: Why vaccinate if chickenpox is a mild illness?
faq.a: In teens and adults, it can be severe. The vaccine also protects against complications.

faq.q: Can I get chickenpox after the vaccine?
faq.a: A mild case with a few blisters can happen. It is much milder than the usual illness.

reminders.text: Chickenpox vaccine tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record.
